en: Oṃ. Of this mantra of the *Śrī-Ṛṇamocana-mahāgaṇapati-stotra*, the venerable Śukrācārya is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Lord Gaṇapati who liberates from debt is the deity (*devatā*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of recitation (*japa*) for the sake of liberation from debt. Oṃ, I remember the Lord of the gods of gods, Vakratuṇḍa, who possesses great strength.
I bow to the gentle one, the remover of great obstacles, for the sake of liberation from debt. ||1||
I bow to the god Mahāgaṇapati, the great truth, the one of great power, the gentle remover of great obstacles, for the sake of liberation from debt. ||2||
I bow to the one who is the single syllable, the single-tusked, the eternal and singular Brahman, who is indeed without a second, for the sake of liberation from debt. 3.
I bow to him who is clad in red garments, who is red in complexion, who is anointed with red fragrant unguents, and who is being worshipped with red flowers—for the sake of liberation from debt. 4.
I bow to Him who is clothed in black garments, who is black in complexion, who is anointed with black perfumes, and who is worshipped with black flowers—for the sake of liberation from debt. 5.
I bow to the one clad in yellow garments, yellow in complexion, anointed with yellow fragrant unguents, and worshipped with yellow flowers, for the sake of liberation from debt. 6.

I bow to him who is surrounded by smoke, who is smoke-colored, who is anointed with the fragrance of smoke, and who is worshipped with smoke-colored flowers, for the sake of liberation from debt. ||7||
I bow to Him who is all-encompassing space, who possesses all colors, who is anointed with all fragrances, and who is worshipped with all flowers, for the sake of liberation from debt. 8.
I bow to the auspicious god, who is of noble birth and beautiful form, who holds a noose and a goad, and who removes all obstacles, for the sake of liberation from debt. 9.
The pure man who recites this Ṛṇahara Stotra at dawn shall, within six months, have his debts severed. (10)
Thus ends the Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, the hymn to the Great Gaṇapati Ṛṇamocana, in its entirety.
